title: Effectiveness of soil remediation intervention in abandoned lead acid battery recycling sites
author: Rahman, Sultana, et al.

steps.title: Collect and process blood samples
steps.instruction: Collect 6 mL venous blood from each enrolled child at baseline and 12‑month follow‑up using trace‑metal‑free certified needles and tubes; transport in a cooler box within 4–6 h to the icddr,b laboratory; aliquot whole blood and store at –80 °C; centrifuge at 894 g for 15 min at ambient temperature to separate serum; aliquot serum and store at –80 °C.

substeps.instruction: Transport blood in cooler box within 4–6 h
Aliquot whole blood and freeze at –80 °C
Centrifuge at 894 g for 15 min at ambient temperature

steps.title: Collect and store urine samples
steps.instruction: Instruct field workers to collect a 50 mL spot urine sample in a Falcon tube; keep the sample at 2–8 °C and transport to the icddr,b laboratory within 6 h; store the urine at –80 °C for future metal analysis (e.g., arsenic).

steps.title: Collect composite soil samples
steps.instruction: At each household, identify five points in the child's play area and courtyard (four corners and the centre); collect ~5 g soil from the top 5 cm at each point; combine to obtain a 20–25 g composite sample; place in a zip‑lock bag; transport to icddr,b and measure Pb concentration with a hand‑held XRF analyser.

steps.title: Collect sweep dust samples
steps.instruction: Ask the household member to sweep the floor with a regular broom; use a pre‑cleaned paint brush to gather the dust; store the dust in a zip‑lock bag; measure the length and width of the dwelling and courtyard with a measuring tape to calculate the surface area of the collected sweep dust.

steps.title: Collect wipe dust samples
steps.instruction: Place a pre‑cleaned 10 × 10 cm frame on the floor; insert a clean, wet tissue wipe inside the frame; wipe the area using an “S”‑shaped motion with firm pressure; fold the wipe in half and repeat the wiping process four times; transfer the tissue wipe to a zip‑lock bag for storage.

steps.title: Collect drinking water samples
steps.instruction: Collect 50 mL of water from the household drinking‑water source into a Falcon tube; deliver to the icddr,b laboratory within 6–8 h; store at 2–8 °C for future metal analysis.

steps.title: Collect turmeric, chili powder, and paint chips
steps.instruction: For turmeric powder, request 10–15 g from the household and transfer with a pre‑cleaned spoon into a zip‑lock bag; if dry turmeric roots are present, collect 3–4 roots and place in a zip‑lock bag; grind all turmeric (and chili powder) samples with a mortar and pestle before XRF analysis; for paint chips, if visible cracks exist, extract chips using forceps and sharpies and store in a zip‑lock bag.

steps.title: Analyze samples with portable XRF
steps.instruction: Analyze soil, dust, turmeric, chili powder, and paint‑chip samples using a portable XRF (Olympus; DMTA‑10075‑01EN) at icddr,b; retain aliquots of dust and soil samples for future analysis.

steps.title: Perform statistical data analysis
steps.instruction: Use Stata 13 (StataCorp LP) to calculate proportions for categorical variables and median/IQR for continuous variables; assess intervention effect on blood lead levels using Generalized Estimating Equation (GEE) adjusting for covariates (Pb‑soldered cans, household members in Pb industry, environmental Pb concentrations, distance from ULAB sites); compare BLL reduction between intervention and control arms; conduct multivariable regression to evaluate associations with cardiovascular, renal, hematological, immunological, and endocrinological outcomes.

steps.title: Conduct qualitative data analysis
steps.instruction: Use ATLAS.ti version 5.2 to import coded interview transcripts; develop a coding system by multiple readings to identify similarities and differences; enter coded data into ATLAS.ti to extract themes and concepts; perform comparison and triangulation across data collection techniques.
